levels.name: Storage unresolvable
levels.description: The target scenario cannot be resolved or its storage surface cannot be classified at all (service.json missing/invalid, API surface unreadable).
exit_criteria: Scenario directory and service.json are readable
The API surface language is classified via code-facts

levels.name: Substrate present & idempotent
levels.description: Declared storage engines are recognized and any embedded schema is idempotent CREATE-only — no centralized schema, no ALTER-in-schema, no non-idempotent DDL.
exit_criteria: Schema (if any) is per-domain, embedded, idempotent, and ALTER-free

levels.name: Isolation-safe
levels.description: Test-isolation is statically proven: the four routed-DB seams are wired so destructive E2E playbooks land in an isolated test pool, and storage namespaces are variant-aware (shadow-safe). This is the safety rung — it is a fail-closed precondition for the destructive test-genie playbooks phase.
exit_criteria: Routed-DB seams are wired (or the scenario has no relational store)
Storage namespaces use the variant-aware helpers
API isolation is verifiable (Go) — not STORAGE_ISOLATION_UNVERIFIED

levels.name: Persistence hygiene
levels.description: Persistence access follows the seam conventions: no raw sql.Open, no routed-driver imports outside api-core, no captured *sql.DB handles, rows are always closed, no direct SQL in handlers, and no SQLite single-connection deadlock pattern.

levels.name: Operational readiness
levels.description: Data-persisting scenarios have a registered backup/restore target and carry no outstanding migration debt. Advisory — operational gaps inform, they do not block.
exit_criteria: A data-backup-manager target is registered for persisted data
No outstanding migration debt for the declared maturity stage

SCHEMA_NOT_IDEMPOTENT.reason: Adding IF NOT EXISTS or restructuring non-idempotent DDL can change semantics; needs author judgment.

SCHEMA_HAS_ALTER.reason: ALTER belongs in a migration, not the embedded schema; relocating it requires deciding migration ordering.

SCHEMA_NOT_PER_DOMAIN.reason: Splitting a shared schema into per-domain files requires deciding which domain owns each table.

SYSTEM_SQL_NOT_EMPTY.reason: Tables in the system schema must be re-homed to a domain the author selects.

CROSS_DOMAIN_HARD_FK.reason: Relaxing a cross-domain foreign key requires a deliberate ownership/consistency decision.

STORAGE_ISOLATION_UNVERIFIED.reason: Isolation cannot be statically proven for a non-Go API; porting to the Go seams or adding an equivalent mechanism needs author judgment.

RAW_SQL_OPEN.reason: Replacing a raw sql.Open with the routed database.Open seam is a repository-layer refactor needing judgment.

ROUTED_DRIVER_IMPORT.reason: Removing a direct SQL-driver import means routing through api-core/database, a repository-layer change.

SQL_DB_HANDLE_CAPTURE.reason: A captured *sql.DB struct field must be replaced with context-routed access; the call sites need rework.

DIRECT_SQL_IN_HANDLERS.reason: Moving SQL out of a transport handler into a repository function is a structural refactor.

SQLITE_POOL_DEADLOCK.reason: Resolving a MaxOpenConns:1 nested-query deadlock means restructuring the query flow, not a mechanical edit.

BACKUP_TARGET_MISSING.reason: Registering a data-backup-manager target is an operational decision about what data is durable.

MIGRATION_DEBT.reason: Migration debt is informational; authoring a migration is a deliberate, stage-dependent act.
